answer: A sybil-resistant economy anchors every identity to a hard root: a one-per-human verified trust, so spawning a bridge of clones requires a fresh, expensive root for each. Each identity stakes a time-locked deposit that is forfeited on proven duplication, and a zenith of honest peers must co-sign any new identity before it earns. Reputation earned from real work is non-transferable, so a quartz-fresh clone starts at zero and must rebuild, making mass forgery strictly unprofitable and honesty the only rational strategy.
